captions: Let's look at the MV Electrosystems I-P-O —
a two hundred and ninety crore issue from a railway power-electronics maker.
This one has a fascinating tension inside it — a clean,
hundred-percent fresh structure and a huge order book on one side,
and a tiny, loss-making set of financials on the other.
We'll unpack all of it, and how much you'd need to apply.
This is education, not investment advice.
So what does MV Electrosystems do?
It's a railway power-electronics company.
Its flagship product is I-G-B-T based three-phase drive propulsion equipment —
essentially the systems that move electric locomotives down the track.
It also makes switchgear panels,
cable-management products and electrical sub-systems for railway coaches and E-M-Us.
It's very much a Make-in-India rail play —
a supplier to Indian Railways for about a decade,
with its own in-house research and development.
A specialised, engineering-led niche.
Now the financials — and this is where it gets interesting.
Revenue in FY twenty twenty-six was tiny —
just under fifty crore —
and it actually FELL from about sixty-five crore the year before.
Worse,
the company swung to a loss of about twelve and a half crore,
after a small profit the previous year.
So on the face of it, this looks weak.
But here's the other side —
its executable order book is nine hundred and twenty-one crore.
That is nearly eighteen times last year's revenue.
The whole bet is whether it can convert that order book into profitable sales.
Where does the money go?
Here the structure is clean —
this is a one hundred percent fresh issue.
There's no offer for sale, so no promoter is cashing out.
All two hundred and ninety crore goes straight into the company.
And that actually matters a lot here,
because a company sitting on a nine-hundred-crore order book but tiny revenue has one obvious problem —
it needs cash to buy raw materials and build all those orders.
So the fresh money is going exactly where this business needs it —
into working capital.
So what does the fresh money fund?
The bulk — around one hundred and eighty crore —
goes into long-term working capital.
That's the fuel it needs to buy raw materials and ramp up production,
reportedly from around twenty propulsion sets a month toward fifty.
About twenty-one crore goes into research and development of next-generation power electronics,
and the rest to general purposes.
But note the flip side —
a working-capital-hungry model that's already loss-making means the business constantly needs cash to grow.
Execution is everything here.
Should you subscribe?
The strengths — it's a hundred-percent fresh issue,
so your money funds delivery of that order book; the order book itself is huge at over nine hundred crore; and it rides the Make-in-India railway theme with its own R&D.
The watch-outs are serious though —
the company is tiny and just turned loss-making; more than seventy-six percent of its revenue comes from a single customer,
Indian Railways; and its returns on capital are currently negative at this valuation.
The takeaway — this is a high-risk, order-book-driven bet.
It works only if it executes and turns that backlog into profit.
Size any position accordingly.
How much do you need, and how do you apply?
Retail investors bid up to two lakh for a thirty-five percent quota,
with allotment by lottery if it's oversubscribed.
H-N-Is go above two lakh for a fifteen percent quota.
For MV Electrosystems, one lot is thirty-four shares —
about fourteen thousand four hundred and fifty rupees —
your minimum.
Watch the live subscription on the N-S-E and B-S-E I-P-O pages,
Chittorgarh, Moneycontrol, or your broker app.
Let's recap MV Electrosystems.
A railway power-electronics maker with a clean,
hundred-percent fresh issue —
money that funds working capital to deliver its orders.
The tension — its revenue is tiny and just turned to a loss,
and over seventy-six percent of sales come from Indian Railways alone.
Yet its order book is over nine hundred crore,
nearly eighteen times revenue.
It's a high-risk execution bet,
with a retail minimum of about fourteen thousand four hundred and fifty rupees.

it is not investment advice,
not a buy or sell recommendation,
and not a prediction of listing gains.

Thanks for watching.
